summary.short: French omnibus law (7 Oct 2016) on open public data, notice of algorithmic individual decisions by administrations, net neutrality, data portability, platform and review transparency, personal data rights and digital accessibility.
summary.long: Loi n° 2016-1321 of 7 October 2016 (in force) amends several codes. Title I (open data): administrations must communicate and publish administrative documents and data in open formats, reuse of public information is free of charge under stated conditions, and reference data, court decisions and certain concessionaire and energy-network data become available. Individual decisions taken on the basis of algorithmic processing must carry an explicit mention and, on request, the rules of the processing (Art. 4, new L. 311-3-1 CRPA). Title II (digital environment): net neutrality is written into the electronic communications code; consumers may recover their data; platform operators must inform users about ranking and referencing; hosts of consumer reviews must publish moderation rules; and the personal data act is amended (new user rights, minors' erasure right, post-mortem directives, CNIL sanctions capped at 3 million euros, criminal offences on sexual recordings). Text and data mining for research is an exception to copyright. Title III: accessibility of public and large-company websites, relay telephone services for deaf and hard-of-hearing users, maintenance of internet access for vulnerable households, and rules for esports competitions and professional player contracts. Some provisions have dated effect (e.g., 1 January 2017, 25 May 2018).
